title: Design a Search Autocomplete / Typeahead: Trie data structure, top-K suggestions, pre-computed results, caching popular queries, real-time updates.
keyPoints: A trie indexes query strings by prefix; walking the path for a prefix lands on the node for all completions.
Precompute and cache the top-K most popular completions at each trie node for near-constant-time results.
Popularity rankings come from query logs; update in batches to keep reads fast while staying fresh.
Cache the hottest prefixes (single letters) in a fast store so even the trie walk is skipped.
The trade-off is freshness vs read speed: a new trending query may take minutes to appear in suggestions.
Filter suggestions by user context and permissions so a customer never sees admin-only actions.
The trie walk costs only the length of the prefix, making it independent of vocabulary size.

s1_definition.oneliner: Index queries in a trie by prefix, precompute top-K popular completions at each node, cache hot prefixes, and refresh rankings from query logs.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Trie** : a tree where each edge is a character; walking a path spells a prefix, and the node represents all queries starting with it.
- **Top-K precomputation** : storing the K most popular completions at each trie node for near-constant-time results.
- **Query log** : the source of popularity data; each search increments a query's frequency.
- **Batched updates** : periodically rebuilding top-K lists from recent logs to keep suggestions fresh without slowing reads.
s1_definition.analogy: When Rajesh types "tra" in the National Bank of India app, it instantly suggests "transfer money," "transaction history," and "track cheque." The app keeps a tree of letters where following t-r-a lands on a ready-made list of the best suggestions.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Search Autocomplete Architecture

  ┌──────────┐  "tra"  ┌──────────────┐  HIT  ┌───────────────┐
  │  Client  │────────►│  Prefix      │──────►│ Top-K results │
  │  (typing)│         │  Cache       │       │ (cached)      │
  └──────────┘         │  (Redis)     │       └───────────────┘
                       └──────┬───────┘
                         MISS │
                       ┌──────▼───────┐
                       │  Trie Server │
                       │              │
                       │  root        │
                       │  └─t         │
                       │    └─r       │
                       │      └─a     │ ◄── walk to node
                       │        topK: │
                       │        [transfer money,   │
                       │         transaction history,│
                       │         track cheque]      │
                       └──────────────┘

  Background job:
  Query logs ──► batch process ──► update topK at each node
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
A search autocomplete indexes queries in a trie and precomputes top-K completions at each node for near-constant-time results. Popularity comes from query logs processed in batches. Hot prefixes are cached for even faster responses.

The trade-off is freshness vs speed: a new trending query may take minutes to appear, which is acceptable eventual consistency for rankings. Filter suggestions by context and permissions.

Remember one sentence: walk a trie to the prefix node, return precomputed top-K completions, update rankings in batches from query logs, and cache the hottest prefixes.
